children.label: a
children.prompt: The trapezium $ABCD$ has $AB\parallel CD$, $\angle C=70^\circ$ and $\angle D=50^\circ$. Find the sizes of $\angle A$ and $\angle B$.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles on the parallel lines $AB$ and $CD$ are supplementary:
$$\begin{align*}\angle A&=180^\circ-50^\circ\\\angle A&=130^\circ\\\angle B&=180^\circ-70^\circ\\\angle B&=110^\circ.\end{align*}$$

Prove that the base angles of an isosceles trapezium are equal.

answer.short:
For $AB\parallel DC$ and $AD=BC$, $\angle ADC=\angle BCD$ and $\angle DAB=\angle ABC$.

Construct a parallelogram inside the trapezium and use an isosceles triangle.
answer.worked:
Name the isosceles trapezium $ABCD$, with $AB\parallel DC$ and $AD=BC$. Take $DC$ as the longer base. Draw $BK\parallel AD$ meeting $DC$ at $K$.

$ABKD$ is a parallelogram, so $BK=AD=BC$. Thus $\triangle BKC$ is isosceles and $\angle BKC=\angle BCK$.

Since $BK\parallel AD$, $\angle BKC=\angle ADC$. Also $\angle BCK=\angle BCD$. Therefore $\angle ADC=\angle BCD$.

The angles on each non-parallel side are supplementary because $AB\parallel DC$. Subtracting the equal lower base angles from $180^\circ$ gives $\angle DAB=\angle ABC$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Prove that the diagonals of an isosceles trapezium are equal in length.

answer.short: $DB=AC$ by SAS congruence of $\triangle DBC$ and $\triangle CAD$.
answer.worked:
Name the isosceles trapezium $ABCD$, with $AB\parallel DC$ and $AD=BC$.

In $\triangle DBC$ and $\triangle CAD$:
$$\begin{align*}BC&=AD &&\text{(given)}\\DC&=CD &&\text{(common)}\\\angle BCD&=\angle ADC &&\text{(equal base angles).}\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle DBC\equiv\triangle CAD$ by SAS, so $DB=CA$ by matching sides.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Prove that if a trapezium has equal diagonals then it is isosceles.

answer.short:
$AD=BC$, so the trapezium is isosceles.

Use perpendicular heights and RHS congruence, then SAS congruence.
answer.worked:
Name the trapezium $ABCD$, with $AB\parallel DC$ and $DB=AC$. Take $DC$ as the longer base. Draw perpendiculars $AX$ and $BY$ to the line $DC$.

$AX=BY$ because they are perpendicular distances between the same parallel lines. In the right triangles $DBY$ and $CAX$, $DB=CA$ and $BY=AX$, so $\triangle DBY\equiv\triangle CAX$ by RHS. Hence $DY=CX$.

The perpendicular projections $X,Y$ occur in the same direction along the base as $A,B$, with $XY=AB<DC$. If $X$ were at or beyond $D$ on the outside, then $CX>DY$; if $Y$ were at or beyond $C$ on the outside, then $DY>CX$. Thus both feet lie inside $DC$.

Matching angles of the RHS triangles give $\angle BDY=\angle ACX$. Since $DY$ points towards $C$ and $CX$ points towards $D$, $\angle BDC=\angle ACD$.

Now $DB=CA$, $DC=CD$, and $\angle BDC=\angle ACD$, so $\triangle BDC\equiv\triangle ACD$ by SAS. Therefore $BC=AD$ by matching sides, and the trapezium is isosceles.
